text:
maria: Heads up — we saw a sustained spike in audit events from two large tenants this morning. Ingest queues filled and KMS decryption latency amplified CPU on the indexers. Looking for quick mitigations and longer-term design ideas.

raj: Which part of the pipeline? per-event KMS calls or only for archived payloads?

maria: Per-event envelope key decryption currently happens in the collector before indexing. So every event triggers a KMS decrypt call if it has encrypted fields.

devon: Oof. That explains the latency. KMS calls are ~50-120ms each under load, multiplied by parallelism. Did ingest-bot surface any throttles?

ingest-bot: ingest-bot: 08:12 UTC - downstream indexer CPU at 92%, KMS 429s increased by 18x, enqueue latency > 2s, dropping low-priority events.

lee: Short term: 1) turn on per-tenant sampling for non-critical audit types 2) switch decrypt -> cache envelope key per-tenant for 60s 3) add 429 backpressure to upstream clients with Retry-After header.

anna: Agree. Also we can change the collector to accept encrypted payloads and defer decryption to a separate pool that does batching and uses multi-lingual requests to KMS (batch envelope key decrypt? — not all KMSes support batch decrypt, but we can do client-side envelope caching).

raj: For cost math: if one event decrypt costs an API call at $0.0004, 1M events/day => $400/day. With 5 tenants spiking that's $2k/day just for KMS ops. Plus ES ingestion cost.

devon: On ES: bulk indexing reduces overhead a lot. Changing from single-doc PUTs to _bulk with 5k docs per request dropped our index CPU by ~40% in staging. Also use ILM to roll indexes and reduce warm segment count.

maria: Proposal: immediate flags: sampling 50% for audit.type=metric (non-critical), enable envelope-key LRU cache in collectors (ttl=60s), and switch collector -> DLQ on prolonged KMS 429s. Medium-term: add a decrypter service that consumes encrypted events from Kafka and does batch-aware decryption.

lee: We should also provide a customer-facing note: "We may sample non-essential audit events during sustained spikes to protect availability" — get legal + compliance sign-off.

anna: Schema change note: if we defer decrypting, we need a stable field indicating encryption metadata: `encrypted_v1: { key_id, algo, envelope_id }` so validators and customers can still assert presence/absence. Add to schema registry as optional.

raj: How about indexing strategy to lower cost: compress audit payloads (store raw gzipped blob in S3 + index metadata in ES) so ES index size shrinks. Searchable fields remain as mappings. That reduces storage cost dramatically.

devon: Ops action items: add per-tenant ingress quotas and soft throttles; implement `Retry-After` header on 429; add metrics for KMS latency per-tenant; create runbook for KMS surge (circuit-breaker).

maria: Quick CLI example for bulk ingest we can share with SDK teams:
```
curl -XPOST https://collector.redwood.ai/v1/audit/bulk \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-ndjson' \
  --data-binary @batch.ndjson
```

devon: Also recommend a cost/benefit: 1) envelope cache + async decrypter (~2 engineers, 3w) likely reduces KMS ops by 70-90% and latency by similar. 2) Sampling + DLQ is near-zero infra but loses fidelity. Need PM call for retention SLAs.

lee: I'll draft a short customer communication and a compliance note. maria, can you own rollout plan for the cache + sampling flags?

maria: Yep — I'll create a PR with config flags for tenant sampling rates and the envelope-key cache. Will ping infra to prioritize a temporary KMS quota bump while we deploy.

ops-bot: ops-bot: created ticket #INC-2198 "Audit ingest surge: KMS and backpressure mitigations" assigned to @maria and @devon

raj: One more thought — for super-high-volume tenants we should offer an "ingest-only" contract where data is sent encrypted-at-rest and customers provide an HSM-wrapped key so our infra doesn't call external KMS per-event. This reduces cost and compliance scope.

maria: Good idea. I'll add pricing/contract note to INC-2198. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
